title: Border and Contact
premise: Wendell Eriksen, a veteran air-crash investigator still haunted by the unexplained loss of her family in seat row twelve, is approached by a stranger named Callum Voss who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. He demands repayment: extract a Russian aviation engineer, Ilona Sarkova, who is defecting with proof that a defense contractor falsified flight-control data, the same data Wendell has spent twenty years chasing. Wendell agrees, not for Voss but for the truth, and pulls her estranged protégé Marcus into an operation that unravels into a trap — Sarkova is bait, dangled by the contractor's fixer, Deputy Director Anneke Roos, to flush out every investigator who ever doubted the official record. Wendell must choose between delivering Sarkova to justice and saving Marcus when the extraction turns violent, and in the end she burns her career, exposes the falsified data through a public crash-reconstruction hearing, and learns the truth about row twelve: her family's flight was the contractor's first test. Justice arrives outside the law, but it costs her everything except the one thing she never expected to keep — a future with Sarkova, the woman she was sent to retrieve and instead set free.
about_author: Paloma Joubert is the pen name of a former aviation-safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports before turning to fiction. She lives near the North Sea coast, where she walks the dunes plotting thrillers about people who read black boxes for a living.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Twenty years after the crash that killed her family, Wendell closes her latest investigation with a verdict she doesn't believe. The chapter establishes her ritual of visiting the crash memorial and her suspicion that the flight-control record was altered. Emotional beat: grief calcified into procedure.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Callum Voss appears at a conference bar, thanking Wendell for pulling him from a burning wreck in Marseilles — an event she cannot recall. He leaves a dossier and a deadline. Wendell checks the Marseilles manifest and finds her own signature on a rescue log she never signed. Emotional beat: uncanny unease.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Voss explains the debt: someone staged the rescue to create leverage, and now the debt is called. He wants Wendell to extract Ilona Sarkova, a flight-systems engineer defecting from a Russian subcontractor with proof of falsified certification data. Wendell refuses — until she recognizes the aircraft model from row twelve. Emotional beat: reluctant ignition of purpose.

chapters.title: The Protégé
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Wendell recruits her estranged former protégé, now a freight-logistics fixer with his own grudges against the system. Their reunion is prickly; Marcus agrees only because Wendell once covered for him. They plan the extraction route through Rotterdam. Emotional beat: guarded reconnection.

chapters.title: What Sarkova Carries
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, reviewing Sarkova's smuggled files: test data showing the contractor, Meridian Aerostructures, falsified control-surface response curves. Wendell finds an anomaly in the archive — a 2004 flight test matching her family's aircraft tail number. Emotional beat: the past reaching up through the data.

chapters.title: Deputy Director Roos
chapters.summary: Anneke Roos's POV. The contractor's inside woman at the aviation authority learns Sarkova is moving and orders the extraction watched, not stopped — the defector is bait to identify every skeptic still alive. Roos's cold competence and her own buried complicity are established. Emotional beat: corruption as quiet routine.

chapters.title: Rotterdam, Rain
chapters.summary: Wendell and Marcus make contact with Sarkova in a container terminal safehouse. Sarkova is sharp, frightened, and refuses to hand over the full archive until she's across a border. First sparks of trust — and something more — between her and Wendell. Emotional beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Tail Number
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Cross-referencing Sarkova's data, Wendell confirms Meridian's falsified curves were flight-tested on the exact airframe that became row twelve's aircraft. The crash was not an anomaly; it was a known risk signed off. Emotional beat: grief detonating into rage.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus tails Voss and finds him meeting Roos's security chief — Voss is playing both sides, though for whose benefit is unclear. Marcus confronts him; Voss claims he's feeding the enemy disinformation. Wendell must decide whether to abort. Emotional beat: betrayal's vertigo.

chapters.title: The Extraction
chapters.summary: The team moves Sarkova through the port at night. It goes wrong: Meridian's contractors were waiting, tipped by a leak in the route. Marcus is captured covering the escape; Wendell and Sarkova get out with only half the archive. Emotional beat: action climax of act two, guilt and adrenaline.

chapters.title: Bait Confirmed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Evidence shows the leak was engineered — Sarkova's defection was never secret; she was released like a tagged animal. Wendell tells her. Sarkova's fury and shame crack the alliance until Wendell admits why she's really here: row twelve. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared ruin.

chapters.title: Roos Offers a Trade
chapters.summary: Roos's POV. Roos contacts Wendell directly: Marcus for the archive and Sarkova's silence, framed as mercy. Wendell pretends to consider, buying time. Roos reflects on how many small compromises built her power. Emotional beat: the seduction of complicity.

chapters.title: The Half Archive
chapters.summary: Wendell and Sarkova decrypt the partial data and reconstruct the falsified test sequence — enough to prove the fraud, but not enough to survive cross-examination. They need the second half, which Meridian keeps in an authority data center Roos controls. Emotional beat: the trap's geometry becomes visible.

chapters.title: What Voss Owes
chapters.summary: Voss's POV revealed: the staged Marseilles rescue was Roos's long game, but Voss flipped years ago and has been building a case of his own. He offers Wendell access codes to the data center in exchange for including his evidence. Emotional beat: the double agent's lonely arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Wendell trades a decoy drive for Marcus at an airfield. Roos's people discover the decoy within minutes; Marcus, freed but marked, calls Wendell with a warning before the line goes dead — Roos is moving the operation's endgame to a crash-reconstruction hearing she intends to stage-manage. Emotional beat: rescue shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Hearing Day
chapters.summary: Roos's POV. The authority convenes a public review of the Sarkova allegations, designed to debunk them and close the file forever. Roos has rehearsed every witness — except one. Wendell requests investigator standing using her twenty-year record. Emotional beat: the machine confident in its own weight.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Under oath, Wendell walks the panel through the falsified response curves, then produces the tail number of row twelve's aircraft. The room shifts; Roos's procedural counterattacks begin, and Wendell's credentials are threatened with revocation. Emotional beat: a career burning as fuel.

chapters.title: Sarkova Takes the Stand
chapters.summary: Sarkova, supposedly absent and silenced, appears with the second archive half — Voss's codes got Marcus in the night before. She testifies to Meridian's test-floor fraud in detail. Roos orders the hearing suspended on security grounds. Emotional beat: truth landing like a hammer.

chapters.title: The Rooftop
chapters.summary: Roos, exposed, attempts to destroy the archive and flee via the authority's helipad. Wendell and Marcus intercept her; Voss arrives with recorded evidence of Roos's earlier order to let row twelve's risk stand. Roos's fall is not violent but total — arrest by her own colleagues. Emotional beat: power collapsing inward.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The legal aftermath is messy: Meridian settles, prosecutors slow-walk, and Voss vanishes. Marcus realizes the hearing worked not because the system was just but because Wendell made silence more expensive than truth. He and Wendell part as equals. Emotional beat: earned reconciliation.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Kept
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The full archive reveals the final record: a 2004 memo noting the row-twelve airframe's anomaly and the decision to proceed. Wendell reads it in the memorial chapel and finally lets herself grieve. Emotional beat: catharsis after twenty frozen years.

chapters.title: Border and Contact
chapters.summary: Wendell and Sarkova at a coastal airfield, passports in hand, deciding where to go now that duty has no more claims. Sarkova asks what Wendell will do with the rest of her life; Wendell says, for the first time, she doesn't need a case to answer that. Emotional beat: love as the border finally crossed.
